reviewed_hunks.quote: **Methods.** PRISMA 2020 systematic umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses, supplemented by landmark RCTs. PubMed (1,495-review corpus plus ten scoping searches), OpenAlex citation chasing, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Crossref metadata verification. 2,360 unique bibliographic records and 363 trial records were screened; 105 records (83 primary, 22 context) and 266 outcomes were extracted, including November 2026 updates of six gaming-disorder engagement records, three photosensitivity safety records, one gamification record, three incentive-design records, three goal-setting records, two retrieval-practice records, two habit records and one gamification-caution record. Certainty is recorded as reported by the source review; independent GRADE was not performed.

reviewed_hunks.quote: Three goal-setting records joined the table: specific goals have a large effect on behaviour in insufficiently active adults (g=1.11), and goals without rewards beat goals with rewards (PMID 38560998); multi-component goal setting works (d=0.55) with daily and combined daily-plus-weekly goals beating weekly-only ones (PMID 26445201); implementation intentions with reinforcement increase practice (PMID 30427874). The goal-gradient literature (Kivetz et al., primary studies, narrative-only) adds the mechanism: effort accelerates as the distance to the goal shrinks, which is why the app nudges hardest exactly one session short of the goal. Implemented as R40: one explicit weekly practice-day goal (default 3, adjustable 1-7) with progress display, a one-more-hits-it gradient nudge, and a met-goal acknowledgment that names rest as earned. The bar renders progress visually, like the stamp cards the goal-gradient studies used. The per-session when-where intention is the daily companion; the weekly goal is the reinforcement loop around it.
